name: Lossarnach Captain
oracle_text:
First strike
Whenever this creature or another Human you control enters, tap target creature an opponent controls.
At the beginning of your upkeep, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.
blocked_sentences: At the beginning of your upkeep, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.

needs.what: A token-pool entry for a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token carrying BOTH printed subtypes -- `human_soldier_1_1_w` with types [Creature], subtypes [Human, Soldier], colors [W], power 1, toughness 1, is_token true -- alongside its `data/catalog/registry_images.json` and `data/art/manifest.json` entries, so `create_token` can name the token this card actually prints. This is the card's only blocker: the trigger (`upkeep`) and the effect (`create_token`) both already exist, so the whole card lands the moment the pool entry does.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The pool has exactly two near misses and each drops one printed subtype: `human_1_1_w` (data/cards/zurgo.cards.json:147) is Human only and `soldier_1_1_w` (data/cards/isperia.cards.json:1361) is Soldier only. There is no `human_soldier_1_1_w` anywhere in data/cards/. On this card the dropped subtype is not cosmetic in either direction. Picking `soldier_1_1_w` breaks the card's own engine: its second ability is a `permanent_enters` trigger filtered on `subtypes: [Human]`, so a token that is not a Human would fail to trigger the tap that the printed card triggers every upkeep. Picking `human_1_1_w` keeps that loop but silently costs the Soldier subtype, which other cards read through `subtypes` selectors and Soldier tribal counts. Note that no gate would catch either substitution -- `fidelity.py` measures whether an ability's `text` covers its printed line and never inspects which token id an effect names, and the corpus already contains this approximation (bastion_of_remembrance in data/cards/zurgo.cards.json prints "create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token" and creates `human_1_1_w`, with its ability text trimmed to "create a 1/1 white Human." to match). That is precisely the quietly-wrong outcome to avoid, so the card is held rather than approximated.

notes: The other two printed lines are fully expressible and need nothing new. `first_strike` is in `keywords` and is already in the packet's starting_point. "Whenever this creature or another Human you control enters, tap target creature an opponent controls." is a single `permanent_enters` trigger with `controller: you` and `filter: {subtypes: [Human]}` -- the card is itself a Human, so that one filter covers both halves of the printed clause -- driving `tap` against a target selector of `{zone: battlefield, controller: opponent, types: [Creature]}`. That shape is already proven in the corpus by beregond_of_the_guard (data/authoring/answers/beregond_of_the_guard.json), whose expectation confirms `permanent_enters` also fires for the source's own entry. Duplicate of the third need already filed in data/authoring/gaps/faramir_steward_of_gondor.json, filed again under the same `human_soldier_token` slug so the two group; there it was minor next to a monarch blocker, here it is the sole blocker, which makes it the cheapest gap on the roadmap to close.
